text:
caroline: Heads up - onboarding quickstart reproducible hang. Pagination stops after auth refresh storms + 429s.

sam_k: That sounds nasty. Which sample and SDK?

caroline: node sample in docker image used for workshops. Bundled @redwood/sdk-js v0.7.1. Flow: long-running paginator streaming pages; token expires -> client refreshes auth (3x parallel refresh requests), server returns 429s for those, client backoff then paginator stops emitting for ~20s.

kevin_s: Interesting. So auth refresh creates extra requests that consume throttling tokens?

caroline: Exactly. Logs show refresh requests hit /auth/refresh and are counted against API quota by our edge. Token-bucket sees burst, drains, then paginator workers block waiting for tokens.

sam_k: Can you paste the trimmed logs?

caroline: ```
[2026-04-08T09:12:01Z] INFO auth: refreshing token (exp=0)
[2026-04-08T09:12:01Z] WARN http: 429 x-retry-after=1 /auth/refresh
[2026-04-08T09:12:01Z] INFO throttle: tokens=0
[2026-04-08T09:12:02Z] INFO retry: sleeping 1000ms attempt=1
[2026-04-08T09:12:03Z] INFO throttle: refill +1 (tokens=1)
[2026-04-08T09:12:23Z] INFO paginator: waiting for lease
```

caroline: Note we get a fast refill but paginator doesn't resume for a long time. Looks like semaphore/lease logic requires >1 token or trusts backoff state.

kevin_s: Which SDK behavior in 0.7 causes that? I recall token-bucket was global and some ops grabbed multiple tokens per-call. Also auth refresh raced across workers before we added a refresh-in-flight dedupe.

sam_k: Right - two things here: 1) pre-0.8 SDKs let multiple concurrent auth refreshes happen, 2) token accounting could be per-byte or per-request and might require multi-token reservation. Combined they can starve paginators.

caroline: Proposed quick fixes: 1) change sample Dockerfile to set REDWOOD_PREFER_REFRESH_DEDUPE=true (if SDK supports) or bump SDK to ^0.8 in the image; 2) reduce default concurrency in sample to 3; 3) add a small opt-out so auth refresh doesn't count against user-facing throttle (internal edge only).

kevin_s: We shouldn't change server behavior quickly. For samples, bumping SDK in image and reducing concurrency is low risk. Also add a runtime warning if SDK <=0.7 that says "Auth refresh may cause extra requests - consider upgrading or lowering concurrency".

sam_k: Another mitigation is to make auth refresh use a separate rate limiter client-side that has its own token-bucket so refresh attempts don't compete with paginator tokens. Could be a library change though.

caroline: Good idea. I'll open a small PR to: update Dockerfile to install sdk-js ^0.8.2, set DEFAULT_PAGINATOR_CONCURRENCY=3, add a pre-flight check that warns on sdk version < 0.8, and include a repro script that simulates token expiry by forcing short-lived tokens.

infra-bot: Created ticket RD-6120: "samples: auth refresh + client throttle leads to paginator stalls; update image, defaults, add repro" - https://redwood/issue/RD-6120

kevin_s: Please also add a short playbook snippet: "If users see long paginator pauses: check for parallel auth refresh logs, check sdk version, inspect x-retry-after, and temporarily lower concurrency or bump sdk." Put it under devex/playbooks/clients.

caroline: Will do. PR opened: https://redwood/pr/921 - includes Dockerfile bump, concurrency change, repro script, and README note. Asking @sam_k and @kevin_s for review.

sam_k: Reviewing now. One nit: name the env var REDWOOD_PAGINATOR_CONCURRENCY (consistent across samples). Also include example ThrottleConfig for dev vs prod in README.

kevin_s: :+1: once merged we'll rebuild quickstart images. Also let's add a lightweight integration test that simulates concurrent refresh requests and asserts paginator continues to make progress.

devex-bot: Linked RD-6120 to PR 921 and added labels "onboarding" and "throttle".

caroline: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the playbook entry and the test after PR merges.
